title: I can't code, but I built a daily Pokémon card game site with AI: 8 games, packs, grading, and what I learned
author: Minimum_Teaching_188
selftext:
I'm not a developer. I work full time and built PlayTCG.Games in the evenings, using Claude Code to write all of it. It launched on 9 November.

What it is: a free browser game built on real Pokémon card prices. Every day there are 8 short games (which card sells for more, rank cards by value, a top 10, a grid and more). 

Every game you finish earns coins to open packs of real cards, and you can send pulls for grading.  
Stack: Next.js on Vercel, Supabase for the database, and free card data with real prices.

What worked:  
Describing what I wanted in plain English, then asking for screenshots on a phone and a computer to check it  
Having it test everything properly before each release (it caught real bugs I'd never have found, like a grading feature giving old cards the wrong odds)  
Keeping the game logic separate and tested, so new features didn't break old ones

What was hard:  
Knowing what to ask for. Game design and balance (pack odds, coin rewards) took far longer than the code  
Making it look good on every phone size  
Marketing. Building turned out to be the easy part

Happy to answer questions about the process. And I'd love feedback on the game:  [PlayTCG.games](https://playtcg.games)
